pr_title: Add a reset button to individual keybinds
pr_comments:
I'm not really a UX person but this colour choice seems bad. Green is not a colour I'd use for a destructive operation. Especially so given that the "reset all in section" button is also pink.

![2021-05-09-120233_545x130_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/117567914-9aa96680-b0be-11eb-9995-31677f3e787e.png)
Is there a reason this isn't being done using the `RestoreDefaultValueButton` implementation? I'd rather this uses an existing standard.

If a binding has two associated key combinations, the current implementation allows for resetting them individually. While using "the nub" we use anywhere else would probably to have to reset them both. Not that I mind changing to that behaviour.

Also if the nub is added, it might be a bit weird UX-wise that it'll be the only operation that can be performed on an individual binding without clicking on the keybind button. But again, not a UX person, so...
I'd say resetting all and letting the user re-choose seems fine. The yellow indicator also has the added bonus of letting the user know which values they actually have changed

I'm quite stuck on how to go about implementing the changes.

Should I make the KeyBindingRow a SettingsItem? Or do I have to move (or edit the access modifier) of the RestoreDefaultValueButton?
I think moving the sub-component out to be reused may work better. But it's not going to be a super-simple one either way, since we're not dealing with bindables here directly.

![Screen Shot 2021-05-15 at 1 08 48 am](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33922797/118290745-1de11700-b51a-11eb-86d4-af5f8047f844.png)

So while the latest commits do add the nub, there should be a better way in implementing this.

I have started cleaning this up to hopefully get it to a mergeable state, but somewhat lost confidence that this is the correct way to go halfway in. The bindable bool stuff shoved into `RestoreValueDefaultButton` feels kinda bad to be honest. What would work really well here is a plain old action on click, without any of the bindable stuff. Design needs work, too:

![2021-05-17-212357_543x330_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/118544912-33db1b80-b756-11eb-97ee-d7157b93facf.png)

(note how the rows are now significantly narrower than the button underneath them). And the naming is still pretty bad (`RestorableKeyBindingRow` doesn't only have restore functionality in it). But before I dig further I'd like a sanity check that the overall structure can be considered good enough to go or if it needs changing.

For the design issue, I think this can easily be fixed by making the button less wide than its preceding elements:

![20210518 134639 (dotnet)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/118591667-87457c00-b7df-11eb-841b-32352d543aee.png)

Will push this for now and review the rest of the changes.

What should we rename the classes to? BasicKeyBindingRow and KeyBindingRow?

Also the Reset all keybindings should probably have some sort of a confirmation dialogue. Should this be done in another pull request?

issue_context.title: Add "Reset keybind" button for all individual keybinds
issue_context.body: Add a reset button for all the keybinds that have been configured. This makes it simpler for single keybind resets, instead of resetting a whole section of keybinds.
comments: You're asking for a button to reset every single key bind?

Just a reset button for every keybind so we can reset it to its normal keybind
Ex: If I change the screenshot keybind, then I can reset only the screenshot keybind to its regular keybind by pressing the reset button it individually has.

review_comments: This padding was not moved across to `RestoreDefaultValueButton<T>` - is there a reason why? Because I think I know why - you've probably inadvertently reverted a5842130027d8e9560c9311e997c4916ebc35ba7 by merging `master`.
